exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A Phone-free Weekend
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: Our class is doing a phone-free weekend. Are you joining, Tom?
Tom: I'm not sure. I check my phone almost every few minutes.
Lily: That's exactly why you should try it. It only lasts two days.
Tom: What are we supposed to do without our phones?
Lily: Read a book, play sport, or just talk to people face to face.
Tom: That sounds strange, but maybe good. What will you do?
Lily: I'll visit my grandmother and help her in the garden.
Tom: All right, I'll give it a try. Let's compare notes on Monday.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 邀请 Tom 参加班级的无手机周末;Tom 担心自己几分钟就要看一次手机;Lily 说正因如此才该试,只有两天;可以读书、运动或面对面聊天;Lily 打算去看望奶奶、帮她打理花园;Tom 决定试一试,周一交流感受。

questions.stem: What activity is the class taking part in?

options: He has no phone at all.
He checks his phone very often.
He will be away that weekend.

questions.stem: How long does the challenge last?
What does Lily plan to do during the weekend?
options: Visit her grandmother and help in the garden.

questions.stem: When will they share how it went?

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 A Good Morning Routine
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many successful students say the secret is a good morning routine.
They get up early, while the house is still quiet.
In those calm hours, nothing distracts them from their books.
A short walk or some water helps the brain wake up.
Starting the day well often makes the rest of it easier.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多成功的学生说,秘诀在于良好的晨间作息;他们趁屋里安静时早起;在那些安静的时段里,没有什么能让他们从书本上分心;散散步或喝点水有助于大脑清醒;开好头往往让一天剩下的时间更轻松。

questions.stem: What do many successful students see as the secret?
When do they get up?
options: Early, while the house is quiet.

questions.stem: Why are the early hours useful for study?
What helps the brain wake up?
options: A short walk or some water.

questions.stem: What does starting the day well often do?
options: It makes you tired all day.
It makes the rest of the day easier.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Saving My Pocket Money
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Ben: Mum, I really want that bike, but I never have enough money.
Mum: Where does your pocket money go each week?
Ben: I usually spend it all on snacks and small games.
Mum: Try this: put a little into a jar before you spend the rest.
Ben: But saving feels so slow. The jar will take ages to fill.
Mum: Watching it grow will give you a clear goal to aim for.
Ben: All right. How much should I put in each week?
Mum: Start with a small amount, and add more when you can.
exercises.translation_cn: Ben 想买自行车却总是钱不够;妈妈问他零花钱都花在哪;Ben 说大多花在零食和小游戏上;妈妈建议先往罐子里存一点再花剩下的;Ben 觉得存钱太慢;妈妈说看着罐子变满会给他清晰的目标;Ben 同意,先从小额存起,有余力再多存。

questions.stem: What does Ben want to buy?

options: He spends it on snacks and small games.
He puts it in the bank.

questions.stem: What does his mum suggest?
options: Put a little into a jar before spending the rest.

questions.stem: Why does mum say watching the jar grow helps?
options: It gives him a clear goal.

questions.stem: How much should Ben save at first?
options: A small amount, adding more later.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Hard Tasks First
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple way to stop putting things off.
Do not place your easiest task at the top of your list.
Instead, put the hardest job you least want to do there.
To avoid that task, you will gladly finish the smaller ones.
Bit by bit, your habit of delaying important work disappears.
exercises.translation_cn: 这里有个停止拖延的简单办法:别把最容易的事放在清单最上面;相反,把你最不想做的最难的事放在那里;为了逃避那件难事,你会乐意先做完较小的任务;一点一点地,你拖延重要工作的习惯就消失了。

questions.stem: What problem is the tip trying to solve?
What should you NOT put at the top of the list?
What should go at the top instead?
options: The hardest job you least want to do.

questions.stem: Why will you finish the smaller tasks?
options: To avoid the hard task at the top.

questions.stem: What happens to the habit of delaying?

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Keeping My Cool
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: I shouted at my little brother again, and now I feel terrible.
Grandpa: When you feel anger rising, what do you usually do?
Anna: Nothing. I just say whatever comes into my head.
Grandpa: Try counting slowly to ten before you speak next time.
Anna: Does that really make any difference?
Grandpa: By the time you reach ten, the worst of the anger has gone.
Anna: I see. Angry words are hard to take back, aren't they?
Grandpa: Exactly. They can leave a mark, just like a nail in wood.
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 又冲弟弟吼了,事后很难过;爷爷问她生气时通常怎么做;Anna 说什么都不做,想到什么就说什么;爷爷建议下次开口前慢慢数到十;Anna 怀疑是否真有用;爷爷说数到十时最强烈的怒气已经消退;Anna 明白生气的话很难收回;爷爷说那会像木头上的钉子一样留下痕迹。

questions.stem: Why does Anna feel terrible?
options: She shouted at her little brother.

questions.stem: What does Anna usually do when she is angry?
options: She goes for a long walk.
She says whatever comes into her head.

questions.stem: What does Grandpa advise her to do?
options: Count slowly to ten before speaking.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Being Trusted
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Our school once gave out umbrellas that anyone could borrow.
On each umbrella was printed a short line about honesty.
There was no list and no one checking who took them.
At the end of term, every umbrella had been returned.
Being trusted, we learnt, makes people want to do the right thing.
exercises.translation_cn: 我们学校曾发放可以随意借用的雨伞;每把伞上都印着一句关于诚信的短句;没有登记表,也没人检查谁拿了伞;到学期末,每一把伞都被归还了;我们懂得:被信任会让人更想做正确的事。

questions.stem: What did the school give out?
What was printed on each umbrella?
How were the borrowed umbrellas checked?
options: There was no list and no one checking.
Students signed a form each time.

questions.stem: What happened by the end of term?
What lesson did the students learn?
options: Being trusted makes people want to do right.
